source.author: verg
source.text: Tum Danai gemitu atque ereptae virginis ira undique collecti invadunt, acerrimus Aiax, et gemini Atridae, Dolopumque exercitus omnis; adversi rupto ceu quondam turbine venti confligunt, Zephyrusque Notusque et laetus Eois Eurus equis; stridunt silvae, saevitque tridenti spumeus atque imo Nereus ciet aequora fundo.
source.text_original: Tum Danai gemitu atque ereptae virginis ira / undique collecti invadunt, acerrimus Aiax, / et gemini Atridae, Dolopumque exercitus omnis; / adversi rupto ceu quondam turbine venti / confligunt, Zephyrusque Notusque et laetus Eois / Eurus equis; stridunt silvae, saevitque tridenti / spumeus atque imo Nereus ciet aequora fundo.
source.text_english: Then the Danaans, gathered from all sides by the groan and by anger for the stolen maiden, attack; Ajax is the fiercest, and the twin sons of Atreus, and the whole army of the Dolopes. As when winds clash head-on after the storm has burst, Zephyrus and Notus and Eurus, exulting in his eastern steeds; the woods creak, and foaming Nereus rages with his trident and stirs the seas from their deepest bed.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: fundunt se carcere laeti Thraces equi Zephyrusque et nocti concolor alas nimborum cum prole Notus crinemque procellis hispidus et multa flavus caput Eurus harena; induxere hiemem raucoque ad litora tractu unanimi freta curva ferunt nec sola tridentis regna movent: vasto pariter ruit igneus aether cum tonitru piceoque premit nox omnia caelo.
reuse.text_original: fundunt se carcere laeti / Thraces equi Zephyrusque et nocti concolor alas / nimborum cum prole Notus crinemque procellis / hispidus et multa flavus caput Eurus harena; / induxere hiemem raucoque ad litora tractu / unanimi freta curva ferunt nec sola tridentis / regna movent: vasto pariter ruit igneus aether / cum tonitru piceoque premit nox omnia caelo.
reuse.text_english: Gladly from their prison pour forth the Thracian horses and Zephyrus and Notus, dark as night, with the offspring of the clouds and his wings, and Eurus, rough with storms and golden-headed with much sand; these have brought in winter, and with a hoarse sweep along the shores in one accord they drive the curved seas, nor do they stir only the realms of the trident: at the same time the fiery ether falls with a vast thunderbolt, and night, pitch-black, presses everything from the sky.
